name: TX-19
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+25 partisan lean of the district
Republican fundraising dominance ($2.1M plus outside support vs. $31K)
Prediction markets price the Democrat at about 1%
Open seat with no incumbent effect
model.rationale: The district's R+25 lean, the Republican's overwhelming financial advantage, and markets pricing the Democrat near 1% all point to a safe Republican hold; the baseline of roughly R+20 fits the evidence.
model.watch: A late scandal or unexpected Democratic outside spending could narrow the margin, though a Republican loss remains highly unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Jodey Arrington (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
West Texas's 19th District is a deeply Republican seat, with a partisan lean of about R+25, and incumbent Jodey Arrington's retirement does not put the seat in play. Republican Tom Sell has raised over $2.1 million and benefits from roughly $1.3 million in outside support, while Democrat Kyle Rable has raised about $31,000 with minimal cash on hand.

Prediction markets give the Democrat about a 1% chance of winning, and no expert raters list the race as competitive. With no polling available, the forecast rests on fundamentals, which point to a comfortable Republican victory in the low-to-mid twenty-point range.
